tara: Quick Q — planning to share a staging/sandbox GCS bucket with Integrations for a debugging pass. It contains anonymized logs, model outputs from prompt tests, and some fields we hashed (emails, user_ids). Is sharing that internally OK under our data/classification & AUP? @sec-bot?

sec-bot: Heads up: per policy, internal sharing allowed only for data classes Public/Internal/Confidential. Model-generated text that may contain user PII is treated as Sensitive unless fully redacted. If any Restricted/Sensitive data -> need formal approval and logging of who accessed it. See: https://confluence.redwood/security-data-classes (:info: summary)

devon: To add detail — the model outputs are from synthetic prompts and a handful of real user prompts we used to repro bugs. The real ones were limited to email+ts, but we hashed emails. Is hashing enough or must we redact the model response text too?

anita: Hashing identifiers helps but doesn't make the output "non-sensitive" if the model text can re-identify someone (eg quoted email/text). We require either: full redaction of PII inside model responses OR a narrow, auditable access request (timebound + approved) + must store request in data-access tracker. For this case: if any real prompts/responses remain, file an access request. :white_check_mark:

samir: If we open a time-limited ticketed access (48h) and tag Integrations + sign an internal NDA, does that satisfy the requirement? Also who signs off — infra or security?

anita: 48h with ticket + audit log + minimal set of people is acceptable. Security needs to sign off on the access scope; infra implements the IAM change. Please include the bucket path and exact files in the request. Example required fields: `files`, `purpose`, `people`, `expiration`.

tara: Copy. I'll prepare the request. Bucket path is `gs://redwood-sandbox/logs/2026-03-31-snapshot.json` and a small subset `gs://redwood-sandbox/dev/repro-case-17.json`.

devon: Also for the redaction step we can run the quick scanner: `redact-tool --pii-scan --mask-emails --out cleaned.json` before sharing. That should catch common patterns. Will run and attach report.

anita: Perfect — attach the scan report to the access request. If report shows residual PII in model text, either redact or escalate for security redaction.

tara: Thanks all — I'll open the request now and ping @anita & @sec-bot once it's submitted. :)

sec-bot: Reminder: include expected retention & confirm whether Integrations will copy data out of the bucket. Copying out requires a separate export approval. :eyes:
